audit: 2026-09-15 scheduled remote agent (sixth fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-15_f_1a.json through _f_4b.json, two files per module. Split 12 Paediatrics, 12 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 13 Psychiatry and 13 Medicine; tier mix 28 L3 and 22 L4 with no L2 and no L5, taking the bank to 6392 with all four modules landing on exactly 1598. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed L3 sitting 11.96 to 14.25 points and L4 sitting 10.99 to 13.54 points below their per-topic ideals, with L5 at 5.04 per cent in all four modules, that is marginally above its 5 per cent target everywhere, so every L5 cell carried a negative deficit and generating L5 would have moved that tier further from target rather than towards it. The strict per-question argmax remains degenerate for the seventh consecutive fire: with the modules within 1 question of each other the 0.5 point tie-break window barely opens, and simulated directly the argmax pours almost the whole batch into Paediatrics L3 and Obstetrics L3 and would take the module spread from 1 to about 25, breaching the Section 2 requirement that all four modules stay within about 10. This fire therefore allocated 12/12/13/13 to bring all four modules level at 1598 and steered the tier mix by the within-module deficit, which is where the tie-break clause points when it defers to the Section 2 module-balance rule. After publication L3 rose to 35.92/36.36/38.17/37.17 per cent and L4 to 31.54/32.04/34.11/33.04 per cent, with L5 steady at 5.01 per cent in every module. Audit: valid JSON, zero em-dashes and zero non-ASCII characters, zero banned tokens, every question difficulty 3 or 4, answer-length parity max to min at or under 1.35 on all 50, correct letters exactly 10 per letter A to E, source_refs all resolving to declared source labels, at least two sources per question with an Australian source first, reference_ranges keys all valid, vitals in fixed order or compressed to within normal limits, data_table values all flat strings, no doubled data_table, no lead-in guideline leak, no pertinent-negative parenthetical in any correct option, no weight-based dose arithmetic in any lead-in, explanation.summary 3 to 5 sentences with 3 to 5 key points and a specific pearl on every question. scripts/dupe_gate.py --new was run against the 6342 pre-existing questions and initially failed one item, an Obstetrics question on inability to tolerate vaginal penetration that duplicated sched-0915b-obgyn-009 published earlier the same day; it was replaced outright with a question on imaging suspected appendicitis at 24 weeks when ultrasound cannot visualise the appendix, and the gate was re-run and passed with 0 duplicates.
